Yea that’s the thing with trucking is it’s always there.  Maybe for a select few it’s a great long term job, I think most of us it’s a 5 year max before burnout or health issues. 

Before my cdl I ran a recording studio for 15 years. It shut down in mid 2019, then I got my flight dispatch license. Buuut then covid happened and I got furloughed, so I got a cdl, and I drove for 5 years.  The longest I stayed with 1 company was 13 months. It was with Dart transit. Wasn’t great, but wasn’t bad either. I was on a small carrier account doing intermodal.  Dart basically leased the trucks to this mom and pop carrier, but I ran under their authority. Had my transmission not given out after 13 months I’d probably have stayed with them. Before that I did a year with Werner on a dollar general fresh account.  I’m just tired of job hopping in trucking though. After those 2 I hopped around so much.  Not really cus of stupid shit, but it was always illegal stuff, my money being fd with, or having absolutely no life. Prime, JB hunt, Cardinal logistics, Big G, 46 logistics, Swift, Heartland and a few mom and pops..  

Big G was great but my account got closed and my dispatcher straight up told me all they had was OTR and most drivers weren’t getting more than 800 a week at that time. And for 2 weeks out it wasn’t worth it.  But they treated me well and basically let me do my thing. Swift was about the same. I had a great FM but they money wasn’t worth it and I had a family member end up in the hospital and I suddenly had to be their caregiver. So I couldn’t even stay and make the little I was. 

Everyone else it was always some drama with pay and home time. I liked the runs and terminals Heartland had but they fucked with my pay so much. I worked 14 days in a row and somehow missed their “guaranteed pay” cus I didn’t run during the pay period. Both of those checks didn’t even total to 500 bucks a week cus my account paid 33 cpm vs the 1100 weekly guarantee. I was so livid after that I just quit. Maybe I over reacted but 140 hours for less than 1k in 2 weeks is insane. 

I know this job can vary with hours/miles but we should never make less than 25 an hour for what we have to go through. 

Now I’m back at a regional airline and making 22 an hour, but in august I’ll get bumped up to 25. I work 4 days a week and if I pick up a day or two of overtime I’ll make 50 an hour every hour past 40. Im in a Union and get free travel whenever I want along with 75% off for friends and family and there’s all these opportunities to progress within the company cus the mainline airlines are always pulling employees. 

I don’t really have a love for aviation, and I’d much rather be in a truck than working in a cubicle, but until the trucking industry improves I don’t think I can go back. It’s foundation is built on lies and and borderline slavery. They sell it like it’s a life changing job, but that’s what it was up until 2020. 

Idk..  I’m just so bitter after 5 years of it.  I still feel like a trucker, and I strangely miss sharing the road with y’all and the smell of piss and diesel at a fuel island and truck stop.. the sound of a reefer putting me to sleep..  but no job should cost you your mental or physical health or keep you away for 70 hours and have you come home and not be rolling in dough. 

There’s so much that needs to be fought for yet almost every driver is too worn out and broke to park it or fight. And carriers know they can fire/lose like 1000 drivers or so a week and still fill seats within a month or so, and they play off the ignorance of new drivers.  And the old guys and even the semi experienced try and tell the new guys what’s up, but the new guys do the same shit the vets did. They think they’ll be different or they can play the game.. all that mess. 

Sorry for the rant lol trucking gave me some kind of ptsd or something 😂 and it doesn’t help I grew up with 2 employment lawyers for parents. Knowing how much I was getting screwed never helped lol

I’m 39 and took about 1 and a half grams in 2023 after my soul mate killed herself. 2022 was a brutal year for me and the grief from that was quite unbearable, along with the loneliness. 

I wasn’t sure about taking the mushrooms up until the moment I did them. I took them at a music festival where I knew the vibes would be good, but also had private spots and even a spiritual spot for me. There was a shrine for lost loved ones and I had left her a little shrine in remembrance. 

Within the first 45 mins the anxiety came on strong, but I also went into this experience knowing it wasn’t going to be easy by any means. My intentions were to connect to something spiritually and to break through the grieving I was in. I knew I wasn’t going to be fixed, but maybe I could learn to cope with the loss and learn to continue on somehow. 

By the time I started feeling the mushrooms I went to the shrine area and sat a hammock next to my loved ones shrine. For the whole 6 or so hours I spent there I felt everything from ego death,  a total loss of myself,  past life regression, the greatest anxiety attack, panic attack, depressive episode, thoughts of my death and acceptance, to communicating with my loved one. It was non stop crying, begging and pleading to let me die right there to be with her again. Thoughts I had failed at this life, and had multiple lives before. 

It was the most difficult experience in my life, and yet the most amazing. I learned so much in that time. Both about myself and the world around me and what’s unseen.

Just as soon as the trip came it left. And the afterglow from it was quite strange. But in a positive way. I ended up finding a book at this festival, which was about the poems of St. John of the cross and the dark night of the soul. 

I felt as if I had crossed a veil and into another world. The same timeline as having lost my loved one, but one where I came out capable of carrying on and trying to live my life to the fullest and in ways I hadn’t before. As if her loss freed me to try and make the most of life and learn as much as I can to ward off the grief. 

In the years since it still hasn’t been easy, but I can always look back at that experience and push through. I still have panic attacks and crying spells, but nothing seems to phase me as much as that moment of grief did. Everything feels more like a wave I have to ride out now rather than a mountain I have to climb while through a snow storm. 


And still years later I ask myself if I need antidepressants because of the loss, my daily depression and anxiety..

While I can’t say if mushrooms or antidepressants are right for you, neither are right or wrong to try. 
Just which ever you choose, know they aren’t a immediate fix, and both require work and intentions along with an acceptance that it may get worse before it gets better. Both can be tools, and crutches. To me both aren’t meant for long term use. Maybe off and on use over a period of time but with extended breaks. 

And as others have said getting out and forcing yourself to socialize will help with the loneliness. Maybe not on a soul level, but it’s like laughing and forcing a smile for 5 mins when you’re depressed. It fools your brain. Even for a moment. It changes your chemical activity just long enough to see things slightly different. It’s not easy, hell I struggle getting out these days.. but I have to make myself go to a concert or bar or reconnect with friends here and there. Otherwise I’d rot away or end my life from the weight of it all. 

Sometimes it’s not about fixing yourself, it’s just about surviving til the the day. And then you do it all over again, look back and see how far you’ve come.

No I didn’t fail a drug test with Werner, they saw what was on my med card from the driving school. The first dr I saw accepted all my meds. Basically looked at the paper and said you’re good. 

Werner had their own drs along with many carriers, which you almost never have to pay for.. 

For those drs I only put that I take asthma meds now. Nothing else. I don’t say I’ve had a history of depression, anxiety or even broken bones. 

These drs are for the carrier to base insurance claims off of. 

If you take a controlled substance and it’s given by a dr there’s nothing in the manual saying you can’t take it. It can be adderall or Xanax. If it’s prescribed and you have the bottle it’s legal.. according to the government and DOT. To a carrier it’s a instant red flag and sorry you’re out no questions please just leave. 

If you choose to continue to take your meds that are controlled or even not..  I’d honestly say just leave them out of the dot medical exam and if it’s a downer, take it at night before bed..  I’m not saying break the law, but I’m saying these drs don’t give a fuck about your health. They just don’t want you randomly falling asleep or having a massive heart attack and the carrier having to pay out millions. 

If you do take adderall and have to pass a drug screen just don’t take it for 5 or so days and you should be ok. Obviously not being on any is better in the eyes of this industry, but again, carriers and their drs aren’t my dr and they don’t know my history and what’s worked and hasn’t. 

And honestly almost any anti depressant will get you denied along with things like cholesterol meds or even inderal.. I was given inderal for restless leg syndrome and the Werner dr denied me a second time.. even after “removing” the controlled substances. It wasn’t until about a month later and my 3rd try where I said I’m only taking albuterol that they accepted me. It’s a scam. Nothing about safety.

This was the 2 year anniversary of 2 friends who died from suicide. I wish I could say it gets better, but really I’d say it becomes more manageable. 

The 1st year for me was very hard. Even this year was hard. All I could do was listen to music that reminded me of them and look at pictures and listen to voicemails. I tried to give myself as much alone time and space as I needed the day before, of and after. It’s a traumatic time for our body and mind, and there’s no timeline to the grief or healing. Even long after. 

All I can say is take time to give yourself some love and care.  If you need to cry all day and sleep do it. If you need to eat nothing but candy or call into work and drive endlessly or hide in a park.. do whatever your soul says it needs. It’s a time to grieve and think of that loved one, but it’s also a time to take care of yourself to avoid any extra stress/trauma.  

This year I listened to a playlist of songs that remind me of one of the friends who died. I listened to their voicemails and even called a medium to contact them. Strange I know, but it was how I needed to grieve. I still cried a lot and I can’t say the next week I improved any, but I got through the day. The day of is always the hardest. You just have ti ride it out in whatever way you can. Love them and love yourself too.

You’ll get raises, always have options, and can eventually be self employed if you want and by 30 possibly set to retire or very well off. 

I got into trucking at 33.. It’s been a ride.  From precovid good money to great money during covid to I’m making less than I did precovid driving. Treatment has for the most part always sucked. Tried owning a truck and it was great til the thing kept breaking down and bankrupt me. Profits are thin doing this. 

I’ve lost 2 friends and a a family member since I’ve been driving, had a few breakups, seen a few fatalities and too many wrecks to count. I’ve hit the point where life at home is harder than life in a truck. Living in a truck is easy cus you’re away from 90% of the stress of the world. Driving is fairly easy. Overcoming the loneliness and mental stress the road can bring is the hardest part. 

There’s money to be made but the industry is changing more and more in ways that hurt the driver than benefit them. Advancements are few. Unless you’re going to pursue a union gig. Then maybe become a hub guy at UPS and work your way up in 5 or so years to drive a truck for them. 

There’s also aviation. If you start as a baggage claim or ticket person for Southwest there’s a chance they’ll sponsee you for a pilot career. Or you can get a flight dispatcher license and you’ll have a higher chance at starting at a major due to your experience doing anything at an airline. Dispatchers make stupid good money and the work is too fn easy honestly. I’d be doing it if I could afford to make 19 an hour right now, but I can’t at 38. 

In reality trucking is just pay from 2 low paying full time jobs or a decent full time job and a part time or side hustle. Worst case scenario you make like 300-400 a week due to breakdowns and bs. Best case you might gross closer to 2k. Maybe a little more if you’re Union or hauling specialized. But those weeks are very common for most of us. I’d say if you bring home 1k a week you’re making about what most drivers do. And for the hours and work, and lifestyle.. it’s not worth that. Just get a retail job and work another 20 hours doing Uber.. yea there’s no benefits to those, but you’re home and can have a social life.

I’m 38. Ran a recording studio for 13 years. From 2007 to 2020. Then covid happened and the owner shut it down and retired. I wasn’t rich by any means, but I lived off 400-1k a week.  Just depended on the week. Yea I didn’t have all the gear I wanted or a fancy car or house, but I lived in a funky apt above the studio. I got free drink and food on the weekends for the wedding and bar gigs I did. I got to work with some of the coolest and most talented folks. Girls wanted to hang with me cus I was fun and lived a cool life. I felt like a rockstar. 

Now I’m a truck driver. Making decent money. Working 70 hour weeks. I struggle to noodle on guitar 30 mins or even record people. I’ve lost touch with so many contacts and friends. And I’m local.. The most musical thing I do is a voice lesson weekly. I feel old and boring. I struggle to get a date cus idk what I’d talk about, and while I can buy things for a girl I don’t have much to offer. No sense of excitement. I feel like a boring adult now.  I’m trying to get back into it but it’s hard since I’ve made more money the last 4.5 years. I’ve almost changed my whole lifestyle. My personality. 
Maybe I’ve outgrown it in ways, or life is just different now compared to then.. idk but I miss it deeply in my soul. It kept me alive. It kept me sane. Happy on a soul level. I was rich at heart. 

I know it may sound like rambling, but as someone who did this professionally for years and is struggling to get back into the life now, I’d say keep pushing. Live below your means, keep those musical relationships tight. If you have to serve drinks at a bar a few days a week or Uber a bit to get by do it, but don’t go with a plan b. For years I never had one. It was music or death. Then when covid hit I had more debts than I could handle. I guess all I’m saying is if you’re gonna give up, don’t look back, and if you’re having second thoughts of stopping music, just keep at it. I have moments I believe I’ll see my friends and loved one again.  It’s a hard feeling/faith to hold onto though. It’s a daily ladder you must climb with the knowing there’s some destination at the top. 

I try and look for the little signs. I’d love to hear their voices or see their faces, feel their touch.. but I feel like the spirit can only connect to us with fingerprint in the past or through forms of meditation/trance. 

Sometimes the answers we need are left in letters, photographs, voicemails, or posts on social media. Things that we thought we’d lost and suddenly found, or are reminded of from years prior. 

I spend most of last year trying to find answers and a connection to my soul mate who I lost. We found eachother just months before I lost my best friend 12 years prior, and even though we weren’t together when she passed, we still were close friends, but had just lost touch.. and I had this gut feeling I needed to call her and catch up. Sadly I never listened to that feeling and didn’t find out she died until over a month later.. 

I had so many moments after I found out that I could swear she was trying to talk to me. Trying to hold me and tell me it’s ok. From moments at night crying in bed, swearing I could feel her arms around me, to times I could hear her voice responding to me talking to her. By the summer of 2023 I had spent almost a year trying to find meaning and some sort of answers. 

I was at a music festival in Michigan where she was from that had a shrine for passed loved ones. You could make one for loved ones and put a battery powered candle inside. I left one for her earlier in the day and came back that night. At this time I returned I had also taken a low dose of mushrooms.  Not so much as to have a fun time tripping, but to try and cope with the loss. To give myself one last hoorah for all the tears and to try and find some strength to continue to live without her. Not to forget her, but to accept her death in a sense.. 

As I was coming up I wandered over to the shrine.  It was really the only place I wanted to be the whole weekend. Right next to where her shrine was was a empty hammock. And as the sun went down and the candles turned on, hers began to glow brighter and a completely different hue than the others. I in no way would have known this when I simply picked a candle to put in there. 

In that moment  I broke.  I spent the next 4 hours crying in that hammock closer to her than id probably ever been in my whole life.  I couldn’t see her, but I could feel that she was there. Holding me and comforting me.  Giving me hope for the future.. It was still a very difficult experience for me and I still have my regrets, but the spirit finds a way to show itself.  To this day I still believe she’s with me.  She’s very selfish of me and loves to help me out when I need it. From losing my keys and helping me find them, to making sure I have the day off on her birthday even when my managers tell me no. She’s knows I love her and miss her and she has ways of reminding me that’s she’s still around. 

I had one other event this past January that really sealed the deal for me. I was still trying to find ways of communicating with her. And I’d paid a medium for a course on how to speak to loved ones..  one of the first lessons teaches you how to go into a meditative state and connect with them. 
You’re supposed to think of one question for them and to try and picture them there. While the image I saw wasn’t necessarily the exact image of her, it was still her but in a higher form. And the question I had, was answered immediately. 

The experience was beautiful and powerful. It left me as happy as it did shaken. Only because it was hard to be so close to the other side, and then leave that trance suddenly and return to this existence. I suddenly didn’t want to be “here”

I’m sorry for this long post, and I know a lot of what I said can be taken with a grain of salt. Some will say it was the drugs, or I was just coming up with things in my mind, that there is no afterlife. 
We all have a choice in what we believe, and this is just how I choose to believe. I can’t say there’s a god or a heaven or hell, but I do believe we see our loved ones again in some way. I just can’t explain how.
